paired_reference: Every non-truthful cell is paired with the exact truthful counterpart sharing pair, adapter, shock, seed, allocation policy, focal obligation, coverage profile and fallback policy.
findings: Claim fallback reproduces the earlier manipulability boundary: across all allocation policies, 22.2222% of comparable focal completions improve under synthetic non-truth reporting, with mean gain 1.3274074 ticks and maximum 14 ticks.

Coverage metadata alone does not reduce this manipulation: none, focal_only, nonfocal_only and full produce identical claim-fallback manipulation results because the fallback still treats declarations as authoritative.
Neutral fallback eliminates measured focal reporting gain across all coverage profiles and allocation mechanisms by preventing unattested declarations from supplying positive ordering authority.

Reject-unattested also eliminates measured focal gain, but imposes an availability cost proportional to missing attestation: completion falls to 0 with no attestations, 0.1388889 with focal-only coverage, and 0.2777778 with nonfocal-only coverage, versus 0.4166667 with full coverage.
The same mechanism therefore has materially different semantics depending on what an unattested claim is allowed to do; 'partial attestation' is not a single policy.
design_implication: An evidence-aware allocation layer should explicitly separate attestation coverage from fallback semantics. An unattested assertion must not silently become authoritative merely because an attestation pathway exists elsewhere.
research_alignment: BIS Project Inuksuit describes structured evidence packs with provenance, corroboration and calibrated uncertainty as an early-indication layer rather than a substitute for verified supervisory findings. This supports keeping evidence status and authority semantics explicit rather than collapsing them into a single claim field.
claim_ceiling: Synthetic deterministic partial-attestation observation only; no empirical uncertainty calibration, strategic equilibrium, truthfulness theorem, welfare result, systemic-safety evidence, or policy recommendation.
